**Context from the `domain:ui` execution seat** (PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`), filed by the implementer of #6634 / PR #6842. ⛔ Grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

**This is the same stale rung number as #6634, in that module's own test file** — `record-title.test.ts:133` says *"the record-level name probe (step 3b)"*, **seventeen lines above two comments in the same file calling it `4b`** (`:150`, `:245`). #6634 established which is right: four sites in `record-title.ts` number the `objectDef.fields` derivation as step 4 (module docblock `:34`/`:37`, resolver docblock `:377`/`:380`, `deriveTitleField` `:279`, branch comments `:437`/`:442`), and `3` is `titleFormat` in both ladders. ⇒ **`4b` is correct here too; no re-derivation is owed.**

## ⭐ The useful part: #6842's new pin is green *because* it does not scan this file

PR #6842 added `record-title.stepNumbering.test.ts`, which reads the source and checks every sub-step label against the number that file's **own** ladder gives the rung it sits under — so a deliberate renumbering stays legal while an inconsistent label fails. Its scanned set is `record-title.ts` **only**.

⇒ this card's defect sits in the pin's declared blind spot. The implementer said so explicitly rather than letting the green stand unqualified, and named the follow-up shape: **widen the pin's scanned set to the sibling test file.**

⚠️ ⇒ **the fix here is two things, not one**: correct `:133`, *and* extend the pin so the corrected state is held. Fixing only the comment leaves the same drift free to recur in the same file the pin was written to protect. That is the difference between this card and a typo.

**Everything else already agrees** and was checked during #6634 — `InterfaceListPage.tsx:207-237` and `InterfaceListPage.mapConfig.test.tsx:182-260` (1/2 for `nameField`/`displayNameField`, 3 for `titleFormat`, 4 for derivation), `.changeset/6530-…:34` (*"the resolver's step 4b"*), and `plugin-map`'s `ObjectMap.markerTitle.test.tsx:30` (names the rungs without numbering). ⇒ **population is exactly one site; no discovery work is owed.**

And the module it tests states its ADR-0079 ladder **four times over**, numbering the type-aware derivation from `objectDef.fields` as step `4` with `NAME_ISH_RECORD_KEYS` beneath it as `4b` — step `3` is `objectDef.titleFormat`, **a rendered template, not a record-key probe**.

### ⭐ Take the fix that also holds the line — it is one extra path

PR #6842 added `record-title.stepNumbering.test.ts`, a source-reading pin that checks every sub-step label in `record-title.ts` against the number the file's own ladder gives its rung. That pin **deliberately scans only `record-title.ts`**, which is why it is green today.

⇒ **Widening its scanned set to this sibling test file both fixes this line and mechanically holds it** — one edit plus one path in the pin's scan list. ⛔ Do not take the bare comment edit alone; it leaves the next copy of this exact defect undetectable, and this is already the second site.

⚠️ Check what else that widened scan turns red before committing to it. If other files under `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/` cite the ladder, they come into the pin's population too — that is either a bonus or a bigger card, and it should be measured rather than discovered in CI.

### ⭐ The dedup is bounded honestly and should be read that way

The filer used repo-scoped REST plus a local grep (the search endpoint being unreliable), treated objectui#6634's filing-time search as the established reading, and re-read **only the increment since** — 100 rows, `since=2026-08-28T06:54:38Z`. ⇒ And then said the bound out loud: *"that listing was capped at 100 rows, so it is a bounded increment read, not an exhaustive one."*

⚠️ That is the correct form and triage is **not** treating it as exhaustive. If the widened pin above is taken, it closes the question mechanically and makes the bound moot — a further reason to prefer it.

⚠️ This card sat **6 days** untriaged; objectui's first-touch queue has been structurally starved behind objectstack's older cards (objectstack#15476). ⇒ Re-confirm `:133` still reads `3b` before editing — PR #6842 may have widened its own scan since.

## The direction is settled: `4b` is right, no re-derivation owed

`record-title.ts` states its ADR-0079 ladder **four times over**, numbering the `objectDef.fields` derivation as step **4** with `NAME_ISH_RECORD_KEYS` beneath it as **4b**; step **3** is `objectDef.titleFormat` — **a rendered template, not a record-key probe.** The file contradicts itself seventeen lines apart (`:133` says `3b`; `:150` and `:245` say `4b`).

⭐ Independently corroborated **today**: the objectui#7021 seat measured `record-title.ts`'s `objectDef?.titleFormat` read as *"step 3 of the `getRecordDisplayName` ladder."* Same numbering, a different seat, a different question.

⚠️ That same measurement puts `titleFormat` at **line 560**, where this card's context comment cites `:377`/`:380`/`:437`/`:442` — ⇒ **every line number on this card has moved. Re-locate by content**, and re-confirm `:133` still reads `3b` before editing.

## Population and grading

Population is **exactly one site** — everything else was checked during #6634 (`InterfaceListPage.tsx`, its `mapConfig` test, the #6530 changeset, and `plugin-map`'s marker-title test). ⛔ No discovery work is owed.

`Task` · `p3` · `documentation`: **the number lives in comment text and no assertion reads it.** ⛔ No behaviour change. ⛔ Do not re-grade.

⭐ Triage's note on the dedup is worth preserving: the filer bounded it honestly — a 100-row `since=` increment read, declared as *"a bounded increment read, not an exhaustive one"* — and triage explicitly did **not** treat it as exhaustive. **The widened pin closes that question mechanically and makes the bound moot**, which is a further reason to prefer it over the bare edit.

Dispatch order follows in the next comment.

## PM contract review — PR #8656 accepted, flipped out of draft, auto-merge armed

The bare comment edit was refused, as ordered, and the widened scan is the actual deliverable.

### ⭐ The widened scan was MEASURED before it was committed to

Triage's rider was *"check what else that widened scan turns red before committing to it."* It was: **all 49 files** in `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/`, run through the pin's own regexes **plus a hyphenated `step-Nb` variant** the original did not collect. Only `record-title.test.ts` cites the ladder. ⇒ **Not a bigger card**, established rather than hoped.

Two subtleties caught on the way, both of which would have produced false reds:
- the pin's **own docblock** spells `3b` as narrative — excluded from its population by an explicit assertion;
- the `it('0b. …')` / `1b.` / `2b.` **test names** are sub-cases of steps 0/1/2, not ladder labels — kept out by the comment-line anchor, **and a self-test pins that they are.**

### ⭐ The vacuity guard is the best answer to that trap I have seen today

I warned that widening a source-reading scan set is exactly where an empty or mis-globbed list passes silently. Three layers, and one of them is structural:

1. `SCAN_SET` length ≥ 2, contains both files **by name**, excludes the pin itself, every entry present on disk with non-empty content;
2. ⭐ **per-file label floors typed as `satisfies Record` over the `SCAN_SET` union — so adding an entry without a floor is a COMPILE ERROR**;
3. a cross-set floor > 0.

Layer 2 means the **next** widening cannot be done vacuously either. That is a guard against the class, not just against this instance. And both failure modes were proven, not asserted: **V1** (empty set) and **V2** (mis-pathed entry) each redden, with V1's report stating plainly that *"the per-file loop is vacuous over an empty set, which is why the guard exists."*

### ⭐ R1 is the non-regression axis doing precisely what it was written for

The plausible wrong fix is to reconcile the contradiction by renumbering the **module** so the stray `3b` becomes right. Run **consistently** — 3 ladder sites, `4b`→`3b`, precedence step 4→3 in the module, plus 4 sites in the sibling:

> **every relative check stayed GREEN, and only the absolute pin reddened**: `fields-derivation sites not on step 4: expected [ …(3) ] to deeply equal []`

A self-consistent renumbering satisfies every relative check by construction. That is the entire reason an absolute pin had to exist alongside them, and it is now demonstrated rather than argued. R2 (titleFormat 3→2) behaves the same way.

The caricatures were reported honestly rather than flattered: **C1** (constant extractor) and **C2** (constant verdict) redden **only the fixture self-test** — which is why the fixture self-test exists, carrying the original uncorrected `:133` text so the collector is tested against a known-wrong input rather than against the tree.

Eight ablation legs, **no void legs**, every mutation proven on disk by count before its run and every restore proven by `git hash-object` equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`. LEG D from the JSON reporter across `packages/core/` — 132 files, 2792 tests, zero non-passing.

**Empty-frontmatter changeset**, verdict quoted — correct here: a comment and a test file under a released package's tree, declared as releasing nothing.

And the closing sweep carries its own control: repo-wide `git grep 'step 3b'` now hits **only the pin's own fixture lines**, with a lit control firing on the same command shape.

Every line number on the card had moved, as flagged; all of it re-located by content, and the numbering direction independently corroborated by the objectui#7021 measurement earlier today.
